newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault says it not a takeover target.
newsitem.headline: Renault says it not a takeover target.

text.p: Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer said in a radio interview on Saturday that he did not believe the company ran the risk of attracting a hostile takeover bid.

"In the car industry's history, to my knowledge, there haven't been hostile takeovers. There haven't been acquisitions of car companies except of those which were in an intrinsic position of weakness that did not allow them to ensure their future. As I do not think in any way that that is Renault's case, this risk doesn't exist," he told Radio Classique.
Renault entered the private sector in July when the French government reduced its stake to 46 percent.
Schweitzer said the risk would diminish as the share price rose, "so everything we do to support or ensure that the investment is good effectively protects the company from any hostile operation".

He reiterated the company's plans to reduce its production costs by 3,000 francs per vehicle. "Our costs are not higher than the average for our competitors, but they don't appear to be in line with what the market expects for tomorrow. That is to say, I expect the price war...to be long-lasting, and that we will continue to have a commercial war even when growth resumes," he said.
